sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: Back in September, we sent 99PI producer Christopher Johnson on a reporting trip to Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 去年九月，我们派《99%隐形》的制作人克里斯托弗·约翰逊去亚特兰大进行了一次采访报道。

sentences.en: And that's where I met Myrna Clayton, at her family home in a very chill, wooded suburb about seven miles west of downtown.
sentences.zh: 就是在那里，我在她位于市中心以西约七英里处一个非常宁静、树木繁茂的郊区的家中见到了米尔娜·克莱顿。

sentences.en: Her parents decided to move here in the summer of 1972, all because of a sleepover.
sentences.zh: 她的父母决定在1972年夏天搬到这里，这一切都是因为一次留宿。

sentences.en: I had a friend in elementary school.
sentences.zh: 我上小学时有个朋友。

sentences.en: Her name is Lacanya Glass.
sentences.zh: 她叫拉坎亚·格拉斯。

sentences.en: And I had the joy of being invited to come over to her house for a sleepover.
sentences.zh: 我有幸被邀请去她家留宿。

sentences.en: And we had so much fun playing.
sentences.zh: 我们一起玩得非常开心。

sentences.en: I mean, what do second graders do?
sentences.zh: 我是说，二年级的孩子能玩什么呢？

sentences.en: You don't know what second grade girls do.
sentences.zh: 你不知道二年级的女孩会玩什么。

sentences.en: You run around and play.
sentences.zh: 就是跑来跑去地玩。

sentences.en: And getting to Lacanya's house was magical.
sentences.zh: 去拉坎亚家的路程简直像是一场奇幻之旅。

sentences.en: At the time, Myrna and Lacanya lived in different neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 当时，米尔娜和拉坎亚住在不同的社区。

sentences.en: Myrna's community was a little more dense.
sentences.zh: 米尔娜住的社区稍微拥挤一些。

sentences.en: Her home was nice, modeSt.
sentences.zh: 她的家很不错，很朴素。

sentences.en: And then Myrna's mom would drive her over to Lacanya's.
sentences.zh: 然后米尔娜的妈妈会开车送她去拉坎亚家。

sentences.en: And wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: We had to go through these different streets and around very, it was almost like foresty.
sentences.zh: 我们必须穿过这些不同的街道，绕来绕去，几乎就像是在森林里一样。

sentences.en: And so it was lots of trees and lots of houses.
sentences.zh: 到处都是树，到处都是房子。

sentences.en: And it seemed like the houses, as you got closer and closer, got bigger and bigger and bigger and bigger.
sentences.zh: 而且随着我们越来越近，那些房子似乎变得越来越大，越来越大。

sentences.en: The neighborhood was lush, forested with oaks and hickories and, of course, Georgia pines.
sentences.zh: 那个社区郁郁葱葱，长满了橡树、山核桃树，当然还有佐治亚松树。

sentences.en: The whole ride made Myrna's little jaw drop.
sentences.zh: 整个车程让小米尔娜惊得合不拢嘴。

sentences.en: And it wasn't over.
sentences.zh: 而且还没完。

sentences.en: They'd get to Lacanya's house, go up her driveway, and the entire time, Myrna just stared at her friend's house, enchanted.
sentences.zh: 当他们到达拉坎亚家，驶上车道时，米尔娜一直盯着朋友的房子看，完全被迷住了。

sentences.en: For a second grader, you know, it was like going to Disneyland.
sentences.zh: 对一个二年级的孩子来说，那感觉就像去了迪士尼乐园。

sentences.en: You know, it was just huge.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那房子实在是太大了。

sentences.en: And then to go to the door and ring the doorbell.
sentences.zh: 然后走到门口按响门铃。

sentences.en: Ding, ding, ding, ding, ding.
sentences.zh: 叮，叮，叮，叮，叮。

sentences.en: Little Myrna was so awestruck that she just couldn't stand it anymore.
sentences.zh: 小小的米尔娜被震撼得无法自拔。

sentences.en: One day she came home from Lacanya's and told her father she wanted to live in that neighborhood, too.
sentences.zh: 有一天她从拉坎亚家回来，告诉父亲她也想住在那个社区。

sentences.en: So within a year, we had moved here.
sentences.zh: 所以不到一年，我们就搬到了这里。

sentences.en: So I was a daddy's girl.
sentences.zh: 我可是个“爸爸的小棉袄”。

sentences.en: So my dad made a way.
sentences.zh: 所以我爸爸想办法实现了我的愿望。

sentences.en: No way.
sentences.zh: 不会吧。

sentences.en: So your father, the whole family, put everything in boxes and bought a house and moved for you.
sentences.zh: 所以你父亲，全家人，把所有东西装进箱子，买了房子，就为了你搬家了？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's my daddy.
sentences.zh: 那就是我爸爸。

sentences.en: For Myrna's family and hundreds of others, this community was a 4,000-acre suburban jewel in the post-war South.
sentences.zh: 对于米尔娜的家庭和成百上千的其他家庭来说，这个社区是战后南方一个占地4000英亩的郊区明珠。

sentences.en: It was called Collier Heights, and it was almost entirely black.
sentences.zh: 它叫科利尔高地，而且几乎全是黑人居民。

sentences.en: Just as amazing as the expansive beauty is how this neighborhood came to be, especially given everything that stood in the way.
sentences.zh: 这个社区的诞生过程和它广阔的美景一样令人惊叹，尤其是考虑到当时横亘在面前的重重阻碍。

sentences.en: Collier Heights was established in the early 1950s, when redlining and racial zoning all put hard limits on where black people could live.
sentences.zh: 科利尔高地建立于20世纪50年代初，当时红线政策和种族分区对黑人的居住地有着严格的限制。

sentences.en: So in order to create this huge, dreamy suburb, a team of community leaders used cold, sharp strategy, flipping the logic of Jim Crow housing segregation on its head.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了创造这个巨大的、梦幻般的郊区，一群社区领袖运用了冷峻而敏锐的策略，彻底颠覆了吉姆·克劳法下的住房隔离逻辑。

sentences.en: It was the first time black Americans had the tactics and the resources to build for themselves a modern, middle- and upper-class community on such a massive scale.
sentences.zh: 这是美国黑人第一次拥有了策略和资源，能够如此大规模地为自己建造一个现代化的中上层阶级社区。

sentences.en: If a place like Collier Heights was going to emerge anywhere, it would be in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 如果科利尔高地这样的地方要在某个地方出现，那一定是在亚特兰大。

sentences.en: Black folk have had particular experiences in a city such as Atlanta that have been unique, unlike the American South.
sentences.zh: 黑人在亚特兰大这样的城市有着独特的经历，这与美国南方其他地方不同。

sentences.en: This is a special city for black folk.
sentences.zh: 对于黑人来说，这是一座特殊的城市。

sentences.en: I do not make any ifs, ands, and buts about it.
sentences.zh: 这一点毋庸置疑。

sentences.en: I love this city.
sentences.zh: 我爱这座城市。

sentences.en: Maurice Hobson teaches Africana Studies at Georgia State.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯·霍布森在佐治亚州立大学教授非洲研究。

sentences.en: He has a book about Atlanta called The Legend of the Black Mecca.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本关于亚特兰大的书，名为《黑人麦加的传说》。

sentences.en: And certainly by the end of World War II, that was a well-known moniker for the city, which drew black people from around the country.
sentences.zh: 到二战结束时，这无疑是该市一个众所周知的绰号，吸引了全国各地的黑人。

sentences.en: For close to a century, black Atlantans had been building successful businesses, earning higher ed degrees,
sentences.zh: 近一个世纪以来，亚特兰大的黑人一直在建立成功的企业，获得高等教育学位，

sentences.en: and accumulating wealth and political power at levels few other cities could compete with, especially in the South.
sentences.zh: 并积累了财富和政治权力，其水平是南方其他少数城市所能比拟的。

sentences.en: But this was still the Deep South, and Atlanta was deeply segregated, especially when it came to housing.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然是深南部，亚特兰大在住房方面有着严重的种族隔离。

sentences.en: In the mid-1940s, that system of segregation helped fuel a major housing crisis in the city.
sentences.zh: 20世纪40年代中期，这种隔离制度加剧了该市严重的住房危机。

sentences.en: Atlanta's population was spiking with wartime migrant labor and soldiers coming back home.
sentences.zh: 随着战时移民劳工和士兵返乡，亚特兰大的人口激增。

sentences.en: And those soldiers wanted to, you know, make families.
sentences.zh: 那些士兵想要，你知道的，组建家庭。

sentences.en: Men and women came back from the war, and they wanted to get it in.
sentences.zh: 男男女女从战争中归来，他们想要过上正常生活。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, that's part of it, too.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，这也是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: So we had this population surge, which means now you got a college education, you got a professional job, you got a family you need a house for.
sentences.zh: 所以我们经历了人口激增，这意味着你现在有了大学学历，有了专业工作，有了需要房子的家庭。

sentences.en: Which meant a huge demand for new middle-class housing.
sentences.zh: 这意味着对新的中产阶级住房有着巨大的需求。

sentences.en: But if you were black, despite all that the Mecca had to offer, finding that dream house or any housing wasn't easy.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是黑人，尽管“麦加”拥有这一切，想要找到那栋梦想中的房子或任何住房都不容易。

sentences.en: Because for decades, most of Atlanta's black communities had been strictly segregated and confined to certain parts of the city.
sentences.zh: 因为几十年来，亚特兰大的大多数黑人社区一直被严格隔离，并被限制在城市的特定区域。

sentences.en: Even the black folks with money had to squeeze into just a few segregated neighborhoods with a limited number of houses and apartments.
sentences.zh: 即使是有钱的黑人也只能挤在少数几个隔离的社区里，那里只有有限的房屋和公寓。

sentences.en: All of them are older and is set by a certain number of disadvantages.
sentences.zh: 所有这些社区都很老旧，且受到诸多不利条件的限制。

sentences.en: Andy Weiss teaches history at San Diego State.
sentences.zh: 安迪·韦斯在圣地亚哥州立大学教授历史。

sentences.en: He wrote a book about black suburbanization called Places of Their Own.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本关于黑人郊区化的书，名为《属于他们的地方》。

sentences.en: They're next to heavy industry.
sentences.zh: 它们紧邻重工业区。

sentences.en: They're adjacent to a creek which floods when it rains.
sentences.zh: 它们毗邻一条下雨时会泛滥的小溪。

sentences.en: Smoke and rail lines that cross them.
sentences.zh: 还有穿过它们的烟雾和铁路线。

sentences.en: Range of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: They don't have any services.
sentences.zh: 它们没有任何公共服务。

sentences.en: And as more and more people move to Atlanta, those neighborhoods, existing neighborhoods, are filled to the bursting.
sentences.zh: 随着越来越多的人搬到亚特兰大，那些现有的社区已经拥挤不堪。

sentences.en: Bursting or not, getting out of these neighborhoods was nearly impossible.
sentences.zh: 无论是否拥挤，想要搬出这些社区几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: For starters, the city had carved up downtown Atlanta into residential districts that were zoned by race.
sentences.zh: 首先，该市将亚特兰大市中心划分为按种族分区的住宅区。

sentences.en: At the same time, the federal government wouldn't guarantee loans to black families, insisting they'd cause property values in white neighborhoods to tank.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，联邦政府拒绝为黑人家庭提供贷款担保，坚称他们会导致白人社区的房产价值暴跌。

sentences.en: And on the rare occasion black homebuyers did break through, things could get ugly.
sentences.zh: 而在极少数黑人购房者取得突破的情况下，事情可能会变得很糟糕。

sentences.en: In the late 40s, a black beautician had just purchased her house in a white community west of downtown when it was dynamited, probably by an offshoot of the KKK.
sentences.zh: 40年代末，一位黑人美容师刚在市中心以西的一个白人社区买了房子，结果就被炸毁了，很可能是三K党的一个分支干的。

sentences.en: People who have the capacity to move beyond are being met by mobs, by organized night riders, by the Ku Klux Klan.
sentences.zh: 那些有能力搬出去的人，遭到了暴徒、有组织的夜行者和三K党的袭击。

sentences.en: You know, and they're setting bombs in people's houses.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们在人们的房子里放置炸弹。

sentences.en: Into this world of entrenched housing segregation and terrorism against black homebuyers, stepped an activist named Robert Thompson,
sentences.zh: 在这个住房隔离根深蒂固、针对黑人购房者进行恐怖活动的时代，一位名叫罗伯特·汤普森的活动家站了出来，

sentences.en: who helped find an Enron around the whole system.
sentences.zh: 他帮助找到了绕过整个系统的方法。

sentences.en: Thompson was the housing secretary of Atlanta's Urban League.
sentences.zh: 汤普森是亚特兰大城市联盟的住房秘书。

sentences.en: He believed that housing could be used as a tool for racial progress.
sentences.zh: 他相信住房可以作为种族进步的工具。

sentences.en: In the 1940s, he helped lead an effort to plot out more living spaces for black Atlantans.
sentences.zh: 20世纪40年代，他协助领导了一项为亚特兰大黑人规划更多居住空间的努力。

sentences.en: A lot more.
sentences.zh: 多得多。

sentences.en: Robert Thompson was terrific.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·汤普森非常了不起。

sentences.en: Ron Bayer is a history professor at Georgia Tech, and he interviewed Thompson when Bayer was writing his book, Race and the Shaping of 20th Century Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 罗恩·拜尔是佐治亚理工学院的历史学教授，他在撰写《种族与20世纪亚特兰大的塑造》一书时采访了汤普森。

sentences.en: He was involved in all the discussions that were going on during this time involving where blacks could be cleared to live.
sentences.zh: 他参与了当时所有关于黑人可以在哪里居住的讨论。

sentences.en: And so what the event that Erdly wanted to do, they wanted to set aside areas blacks could move in without meeting violence from whites,
sentences.zh: 所以，埃德利想要做的事情是，他们想划定一些黑人可以搬入而不会遭到白人暴力袭击的区域，

sentences.en: because there was already violence erupting.
sentences.zh: 因为当时暴力事件已经在爆发了。

sentences.en: There was a Q Klux Klan marking around from blacks.
sentences.zh: 三K党当时正在到处针对黑人。

sentences.en: Recordings of Robert Thompson are rare, but in this 1985 interview with Ron Bayer,
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·汤普森的录音很少见，但在1985年接受罗恩·拜尔的这次采访中，

sentences.en: Thompson describes the sense of urgency when it came to housing and violence right after World War II.
sentences.zh: 汤普森描述了二战后住房和暴力问题带来的紧迫感。

sentences.en: There was a hate organization called the Colombians, dynamiting homes of blacks who had moved into North West Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫“哥伦比亚人”的仇恨组织，专门炸毁搬到亚特兰大西北部的黑人的房屋。

sentences.en: So really, you were trying to find housing that you could move into without any kind of violence erupting.
sentences.zh: 所以，你确实是在试图寻找一个可以搬进去而不会引发任何暴力冲突的住所。

sentences.en: Because the town was about to explode.
sentences.zh: 因为这座城市当时几乎要爆炸了。

sentences.en: The town was about to explode, Thompson said.
sentences.zh: 汤普森说，这座城市几乎要爆炸了。

sentences.en: So he and a group of prominent black Atlantans identified half a dozen so-called Negro expansion areas.
sentences.zh: 于是，他和一群亚特兰大著名的黑人确定了六个所谓的“黑人扩张区”。

sentences.en: These were small pockets spread around Atlanta that were very carefully plotted out in order to protect future black residents from violent white backlash.
sentences.zh: 这些是散布在亚特兰大周围的小区域，经过非常仔细的规划，旨在保护未来的黑人居民免受白人暴力反弹的伤害。

sentences.en: The group met with white neighborhood associations, and they struck these so-called gentlemen's agreements to use highways, cemeteries, train tracks,
sentences.zh: 该组织与白人社区协会会面，并达成了所谓的“绅士协议”，利用高速公路、墓地、铁轨，

sentences.en: and other landmarks as boundaries between the black expansion areas and white neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 以及其他地标作为黑人扩张区和白人社区之间的边界。

sentences.en: Y'all stay on your side.
sentences.zh: 你们待在你们那边。

sentences.en: We'll stay on ours.
sentences.zh: 我们待在我们这边。

sentences.en: But these few small areas still weren't enough for a growing black Atlanta, and some of the city's black leadership disliked these gentlemen's agreements just on principle.
sentences.zh: 但这些少数小区域对于不断增长的亚特兰大黑人人口来说仍然不够，而且一些黑人领袖原则上不喜欢这些绅士协议。

sentences.en: They felt that agreeing to segregated boundaries was basically an endorsement of segregation.
sentences.zh: 他们认为同意隔离边界基本上就是对隔离制度的认可。

sentences.en: The irony is, of course, if you looked at the pretty sharply drawn racial barriers around them and boundaries around them,
sentences.zh: 当然，讽刺的是，如果你看看周围那些界限分明的种族屏障和边界，

sentences.en: you would be looking at a map of Jim Crow segregation envisioned to reach out into the foreseeable future of the city.
sentences.zh: 你看到的将是一张吉姆·克劳隔离地图，旨在延伸到这座城市可预见的未来。

sentences.en: So while the expansion areas went ahead, Thompson and his team decided around 1950 that it was time for a much bigger, bolder play.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然扩张区计划继续进行，但汤普森和他的团队在1950年左右决定，是时候采取更大胆的行动了。

sentences.en: One that would harness black Atlanta's development know-how and its wealth.
sentences.zh: 一个能够利用亚特兰大黑人的发展经验和财富的计划。

sentences.en: They called the plan Project X.
sentences.zh: 他们称这个计划为“X计划”。

sentences.en: Project X was the attempt to very simply not have white society where blacks could live.
sentences.zh: X计划的尝试非常简单，就是不让白人社会决定黑人可以在哪里居住。

sentences.en: That was it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: The whole thing was orchestrated by Atlanta's Urban League.
sentences.zh: 整个事情由亚特兰大城市联盟策划。

sentences.en: They'd later write up this document on a typewriter, and the front page just said,
sentences.zh: 他们后来用打字机写下了这份文件，首页上只写着，

sentences.en: Project X in all caps.
sentences.zh: 全大写的“X计划”。

sentences.en: Very special ops.
sentences.zh: 非常像特种作战。

sentences.en: It's sort of a manifesto, sort of a white paper.
sentences.zh: 这算是一种宣言，也算是一种白皮书。

sentences.en: It lays out in cold, hard numbers and charts a crystal clear strategy to grab the west side for black development.
sentences.zh: 它用冷冰冰的数字和图表列出了一个清晰的战略，旨在为黑人发展抢占西区。

sentences.en: Thompson's team surveyed land west of central Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 汤普森的团队考察了亚特兰大市中心以西的土地。

sentences.en: There were some white neighborhoods out there and a few small black communities.
sentences.zh: 那里有一些白人社区和几个小的黑人社区。

sentences.en: But to the west of all those, they saw a lot of undeveloped land that stretched all the way out to the county line.
sentences.zh: 但在所有这些地方的西边，他们看到了大片未开发的土地，一直延伸到县界。

sentences.en: And they decide that they're going to try to buy land further to the weSt.
sentences.zh: 他们决定尝试购买更西边的土地。

sentences.en: Thompson will survey all of the property ownership in a swath of west Atlanta all the way to the Chattahoochee River.
sentences.zh: 汤普森将调查亚特兰大西部一直到查塔胡奇河一带的所有土地所有权。

sentences.en: And they'd find ways to buy up that land and develop it.
sentences.zh: 他们会想办法买下那片土地并进行开发。

sentences.en: Since those parcels were outside the city limits, they weren't subject to Atlanta's race-based zoning laws,
sentences.zh: 由于这些地块在城市范围之外，它们不受亚特兰大基于种族的分区法律的约束，

sentences.en: meaning black people could still buy it if the owners were willing to sell.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果业主愿意出售，黑人仍然可以购买。

sentences.en: Thompson's team needed a strategy.
sentences.zh: 汤普森的团队需要一个策略。

sentences.en: And what they came up with was a plan to use racism in the real estate market to their advantage.
sentences.zh: 他们想出的计划是利用房地产市场中的种族主义为自己谋利。

sentences.en: White Atlantians in the west side were fearful of the arrival of African Americans.
sentences.zh: 西区的白人亚特兰大人对非裔美国人的到来感到恐惧。

sentences.en: The Project X team knew that because they were black, they could depress the value of white-owned space by simply buying property that was adjacent.
sentences.zh: X计划团队知道，因为他们是黑人，他们可以通过购买相邻的房产来压低白人拥有空间的价值。

sentences.en: The white owner would then likely be pressured to sell.
sentences.zh: 白人业主随后很可能会被迫出售。

sentences.en: And once those white communities found out that there were black people next door,
sentences.zh: 一旦那些白人社区发现隔壁有黑人，

sentences.en: those residents were likely to move and white homebuyers would shop elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 那些居民很可能会搬走，而白人购房者也会去别处购买。

sentences.en: Either way, all of that space would then be open to black Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 无论哪种方式，所有这些空间都将向亚特兰大黑人开放。

sentences.en: Manipulating Jim Crow psychology was just a tactic on the way to creating great black neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 操纵吉姆·克劳心理只是通往创造伟大黑人社区的一种策略。

sentences.en: Project X counted on the fear of a black neighbor.
sentences.zh: X计划利用了对黑人邻居的恐惧。

sentences.en: They undertake to use white fears of integration,
sentences.zh: 他们着手利用白人对融合的恐惧，

sentences.en: white fears of living among or near African Americans against whites to secure ownership of land and space for Atlanta's African American west side to grow.
sentences.zh: 利用白人对与非裔美国人共同生活或居住在附近的恐惧，来确保亚特兰大非裔美国人西区的土地和空间所有权，以实现增长。

sentences.en: But they had to keep Project X kind of on the low.
sentences.zh: 但他们必须让X计划保持低调。

sentences.en: White communities were expanding too.
sentences.zh: 白人社区也在扩张。

sentences.en: And if they sensed that black developers wanted this land, they might snatch it up first, effectively cutting off the west side to black people.
sentences.zh: 如果他们感觉到黑人开发商想要这片土地，他们可能会先抢走，从而有效地切断黑人进入西区的途径。

sentences.en: One of Project X's first big steps was to assemble a group of 23 investors, including a few doctors, some teachers, a newspaper editor, and a housewife.
sentences.zh: X计划的首要大动作之一是召集了23名投资者，包括几名医生、一些教师、一名报纸编辑和一名家庭主妇。

sentences.en: They formed a corporation, sold shares to raise money, and set their sights on more than a thousand acres.
sentences.zh: 他们成立了一家公司，通过出售股份筹集资金，并将目标锁定在超过一千英亩的土地上。

sentences.en: And then they went deep into the west side and just started buying up land next to white communities, which were caught completely unawares.
sentences.zh: 然后他们深入西区，开始在白人社区旁边买地，而白人社区对此完全没有察觉。

sentences.en: The white ignorance of the black community, what they didn't know, there was money in the black community.
sentences.zh: 白人对黑人社区的无知在于，他们不知道黑人社区里其实是有钱的。

sentences.en: And they began to jump over the white areas and create housing for themselves beyond that.
sentences.zh: 他们开始跳过白人区域，在白人区域之外为自己创造住房。

sentences.en: So they began to encapsulate the white areas between two black areas.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始将白人区域包裹在两个黑人区域之间。

sentences.en: So the squeeze was on.
sentences.zh: 于是，挤压开始了。

sentences.en: Where the old plan for expansion areas had black neighborhoods surrounded by white homes, Project X flipped that.
sentences.zh: 过去那种将黑人社区包围在白人住宅区中的扩张规划，在“X计划”中被彻底颠覆了。

sentences.en: Black developers were now encircling white communities.
sentences.zh: 现在轮到黑人开发商去包围白人社区了。

sentences.en: In neighborhoods around West Atlanta, locals started seeing these modern, gleaming, new middle-class houses go up on what used to be farmland or woods.
sentences.zh: 在亚特兰大西部的周边社区，当地人开始看到这些现代、闪亮、全新的中产阶级住宅，在曾经的农田或林地上拔地而起。

sentences.en: White homeowners then watched in amazement as black families moved in.
sentences.zh: 白人房主们惊愕地看着黑人家庭搬了进来。

sentences.en: In just a couple of years, multiple white neighborhoods found themselves encircled.
sentences.zh: 仅仅几年时间，多个白人社区就发现自己被包围了。

sentences.en: Robert Thompson described this strategy as both a leapfrog and a military-style pincer move.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·汤普森将这一策略描述为一种“蛙跳”战术和军事风格的“钳形攻势”。

sentences.en: What we were developing at that time was kind of a leapfrog, pincer move.
sentences.zh: 我们当时正在开发的，就是一种类似于蛙跳的钳形攻势。

sentences.en: So what we did, we jumped over.
sentences.zh: 所以我们所做的，就是跳过中间区域。

sentences.en: So then these whites were pocketed.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，这些白人就被困在了中间。

sentences.en: And we had jumped over and bought land.
sentences.zh: 我们跳过他们，买下了土地。

sentences.en: Nobody can stop you from buying land, Thompson said.
sentences.zh: 汤普森说，没人能阻止你买地。

sentences.en: The Project X strategy helped open up Atlanta's west side for black development.
sentences.zh: “X计划”的策略帮助亚特兰大西区打开了黑人开发的大门。

sentences.en: The pincer moves had worked brilliantly.
sentences.zh: 这种钳形攻势取得了辉煌的成功。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, I would say that was right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，没错，我觉得你说得很对。

sentences.en: Very good description coming out of the World War II era.
sentences.zh: 这是对二战时期战术非常好的描述。

sentences.en: The World War II generals would have been proud.
sentences.zh: 二战时期的将军们一定会引以为傲。

sentences.en: It came around the white area and caught them in between.
sentences.zh: 它绕过了白人区域，将他们夹在中间。

sentences.en: And it will produce some of the most attractive, comfortable, expensive, as well as affordable,
sentences.zh: 它将创造出最迷人、最舒适、最昂贵，同时也最实惠的住宅，

sentences.en: suburban-style housing that African Americans are able to purchase and live in anywhere in the United States in the 1950s and 60s.
sentences.zh: 让非裔美国人在20世纪50和60年代的美国任何地方都能买得起并住进去，这就是郊区风格的住宅。

sentences.en: One of the places where these leapfrog tactics were used to best effect was out near a small suburb that was the original, all-white, Collier Heights.
sentences.zh: 这些“蛙跳”战术应用效果最好的地方之一，是在一个小郊区附近，那就是最初全由白人组成的科利尔高地。

sentences.en: In 1953, a black development company bought 1,000 acres west of that white neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 1953年，一家黑人开发公司在那个白人社区的西边买下了1000英亩土地。

sentences.en: And the white folks lost it.
sentences.zh: 白人们彻底慌了。

sentences.en: Rumors spread that the whole area, including their neighborhood of 135 homes, would soon be all black.
sentences.zh: 谣言四起，说整个地区，包括他们那135户住宅的社区，很快就会变成全黑人区。

sentences.en: They understood that if just one person sold, white Collier Heights would fall like dominoes.
sentences.zh: 他们明白，只要有一个人卖房，白人科利尔高地就会像多米诺骨牌一样倒下。

sentences.en: The small community tried to form a united front.
sentences.zh: 这个小社区试图建立统一战线。

sentences.en: The Civic Club made it a moral issue, pressuring neighbors to stay loyal to the white race by holding the line.
sentences.zh: 市民俱乐部将其上升到道德高度，通过坚守阵地来向邻居施压，要求他们对白人种族保持忠诚。

sentences.en: Those who wanted to sell were accused of being selfish.
sentences.zh: 那些想卖房的人被指责为自私。

sentences.en: As one homeowner lamented,
sentences.zh: 正如一位房主所感叹的那样：

sentences.en: We sure do want to keep our property white, but there are Negroes all around us now.
sentences.zh: “我们当然想保持我们的社区是白人的，但现在我们周围全是黑人。”

sentences.en: In just a few months, every white resident had sold their house to a black buyer.
sentences.zh: 仅仅几个月内，每一位白人居民都把房子卖给了黑人买家。

sentences.en: It was all over.
sentences.zh: 一切都结束了。

sentences.en: White Collier Heights had become a black community just like that.
sentences.zh: 科利尔高地就这样变成了一个黑人社区。

sentences.en: Every house that you see that you're passing now, this was all white.
sentences.zh: 你现在经过看到的每一栋房子，以前全都是白人的。

sentences.en: We call it Cracker Bill.
sentences.zh: 我们管它叫“乡巴佬比尔”。

sentences.en: I wanted to see Collier Heights for myself, especially the front line that was once called Hightower Road,
sentences.zh: 我想亲自去看看科利尔高地，特别是曾经被称为海特沃大道的前线，

sentences.en: and how the whole area changed when it became all black.
sentences.zh: 以及当它变成全黑人区后，整个区域发生了怎样的变化。

sentences.en: Clarence Luckett Sr.
sentences.zh: 老克拉伦斯·卢克特，

sentences.en: was more than happy to show me around.
sentences.zh: 非常乐意带我四处看看。

sentences.en: He's a deacon at Ebenezer Baptist Church, and he moved to Collier Heights in 1959.
sentences.zh: 他是埃比尼泽浸信会教堂的执事，1959年搬到了科利尔高地。

sentences.en: All this you see now, you're passing, did no blacks live up this way.
sentences.zh: 你现在经过看到的这一切，以前根本没有黑人住在这边。

sentences.en: All down through here was white.
sentences.zh: 这一带全是白人。

sentences.en: All down, everything, left to right.
sentences.zh: 从头到尾，所有地方，从左到右。

sentences.en: He takes me past the wood-framed houses that belong to the white community that used to live here.
sentences.zh: 他带我经过那些属于曾经住在这里的白人社区的木结构房屋。

sentences.en: It really is like looking at the ruins of a segregated front line.
sentences.zh: 这真的就像是在看种族隔离前线的废墟。

sentences.en: It's when we turn and head west into Collier Heights that I can really appreciate the checkmate,
sentences.zh: 当我们转弯向西进入科利尔高地时，我才真正领略到那种“将死”的局面，

sentences.en: that jumping-the-whites pincer mode.
sentences.zh: 那种“跳过白人”的钳形攻势模式。

sentences.en: You can see the difference, and we're going to make a left.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出区别，我们要向左转。

sentences.en: You see the brick house on the hill up there?
sentences.zh: 看到山坡上那栋砖房了吗？

sentences.en: Luckett says right there in the architecture is proof that the squeeze tactic was a success.
sentences.zh: 卢克特说，建筑本身就是这种挤压战术成功的证明。

sentences.en: You just keep in mind, all the brick was basically built by blacks for blacks,
sentences.zh: 你要记住，所有的砖房基本上都是黑人为黑人建造的，

sentences.en: and you can see them as you come down to your right.
sentences.zh: 当你向右看时就能看到它们。

sentences.en: These narrow asphalt roads roll and bend under a hunter-green canopy of magnolias and dogwoods.
sentences.zh: 这些狭窄的柏油路在木兰花和山茱萸构成的深绿色树冠下蜿蜒起伏。

sentences.en: We drive by one ranch home, peach-colored brick, a window wall with cream curtains drawn against the sun.
sentences.zh: 我们开车经过一栋牧场式住宅，桃色的砖墙，一整面窗户挂着抵挡阳光的奶油色窗帘。

sentences.en: It sits like a crown on top of a grassy hill.
sentences.zh: 它像皇冠一样坐落在长满草的山顶上。

sentences.en: The lawn is manicured and crisp.
sentences.zh: 草坪修剪得整整齐齐，非常清爽。

sentences.en: And this used to be a cool dude here, and he had a convertible, and he's a Playboy.
sentences.zh: 以前住在这里的是个酷哥，他有辆敞篷车，是个花花公子。

sentences.en: He lived here.
sentences.zh: 他住在这儿。

sentences.en: It looks like a Playboy house.
sentences.zh: 这看起来就像个花花公子的房子。

sentences.en: Yeah, he was there.
sentences.zh: 没错，他就在那儿。

sentences.en: He had a fancy little car, and this was Dr. Roberts.
sentences.zh: 他有一辆时髦的小车，这就是罗伯茨医生的家。

sentences.en: We used to sit there on this porch and talk about everybody in the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 我们过去常坐在那个门廊上，谈论社区里的每一个人。

sentences.en: In the mid-1950s, this neighborhood became Atlanta's finest development for black people,
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代中期，这个社区成为了亚特兰大最优秀的黑人开发区，

sentences.en: where houses went for $20,000 to $50,000.
sentences.zh: 那里的房子售价在2万到5万美元之间。

sentences.en: Today, the most expensive houses would run you more than $500,000.
sentences.zh: 今天，最贵的房子要卖到50多万美元。

sentences.en: By the mid-1960s, Collier Heights was the dream, a modern 4,000-acre oasis.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪60年代中期，科利尔高地成了梦想之地，一个现代化的4000英亩绿洲。

sentences.en: Black suburbanization was happening fast, especially across the South.
sentences.zh: 黑人郊区化进程迅速，尤其是在南方。

sentences.en: But in terms of its sheer scale, its newness, and its status as a middle- and upper-middle-class neighborhood,
sentences.zh: 但就其规模、新颖程度以及作为中产和中上阶层社区的地位而言，

sentences.en: there was nothing else like Collier Heights anywhere in the country.
sentences.zh: 全国任何地方都没有像科利尔高地这样的地方。

sentences.en: Watching this house, my house, my house be built, was exciting.
sentences.zh: 看着这栋房子，我的房子，看着它被建造起来，真是令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Minette Coleman was in seventh grade when her parents had their house built from scratch.
sentences.zh: 米内特·科尔曼上七年级时，她的父母从零开始建造了他们的房子。

sentences.en: Sometimes when my father and mother would go look at it,
sentences.zh: 有时当我的父母去查看进度时，

sentences.en: I got to go look at the progress they were making with the house.
sentences.zh: 我也有机会去看看房子建造的进展。

sentences.en: And every day when we went to school, we took a bus that drove past the property.
sentences.zh: 每天上学时，我们坐的校车都会经过这处房产。

sentences.en: When the Colemans moved in in the 1960s,
sentences.zh: 当科尔曼一家在20世纪60年代搬进来时，

sentences.en: they joined a community of more than 5,200 black Atlantans living in Collier Heights.
sentences.zh: 他们加入了一个由5200多名居住在科利尔高地的亚特兰大黑人组成的社区。

sentences.en: Minette remembers her family's backyard shaded by enormous Georgia pines.
sentences.zh: 米内特记得她家后院被巨大的乔治亚松树遮蔽着。

sentences.en: My cousin would come down from Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 我的表亲会从华盛顿特区过来。

sentences.en: We'd get our books, and we'd read for hours, just sitting under these big pine trees.
sentences.zh: 我们拿着书，坐在这些大松树下读上几个小时。

sentences.en: And then as we got older, we'd sit under those pine trees and talk about boys.
sentences.zh: 后来我们长大了，就会坐在那些松树下聊男生。

sentences.en: Collier Heights came to encompass 54 subdivisions.
sentences.zh: 科利尔高地最终包含了54个住宅区。

sentences.en: Places like Kings Grant, Miami Heights, Crescendo Valley.
sentences.zh: 像国王赠地、迈阿密高地、克雷森多谷这样的地方。

sentences.en: Black Atlantans, who drove out looking for their dream homes,
sentences.zh: 那些开车出来寻找梦想家园的亚特兰大黑人，

sentences.en: would park and take footpaths up through vast front lawns.
sentences.zh: 会把车停好，沿着小路穿过宽阔的前草坪。

sentences.en: They'd tour split-level homes that sometimes went three, four, even five stories down the back of a hill.
sentences.zh: 他们会参观那些错层式住宅，有些房子在山坡后甚至有三、四、五层高。

sentences.en: Collier Heights had a whole rainbow of ranch styles.
sentences.zh: 科利尔高地拥有各种各样的牧场风格住宅。

sentences.en: Compact, linear, linear with clusters, bungalow, alphabet.
sentences.zh: 紧凑型、线性型、集群线性型、平房型、字母型。

sentences.en: Some of them designed by the best architects in the game.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是由业内最好的建筑师设计的。

sentences.en: There were homes with pagoda-inspired roofs,
sentences.zh: 有带有宝塔风格屋顶的房子，

sentences.en: and others designed in a style called the Woodland Master Deluxe Split Level.
sentences.zh: 还有以“林地大师豪华错层”风格设计的房子。

sentences.en: There was one house, it's still there,
sentences.zh: 有一栋房子，现在还在那儿，

sentences.en: built-in-the-round for perfect acoustics,
sentences.zh: 为了完美的声学效果而建成了圆形，

sentences.en: custom-made for the local high school band director.
sentences.zh: 是专门为当地高中乐队指挥定制的。

sentences.en: As for Manette Coleman's home, she can still picture it on the inside.
sentences.zh: 至于米内特·科尔曼的家，她至今还能想象出里面的样子。

sentences.en: How could I forget it?
sentences.zh: 我怎么可能忘得掉？

sentences.en: First of all,
sentences.zh: 首先，

sentences.en: it was back in the days when avocado green was popular,
sentences.zh: 那是在牛油果绿流行的年代，

sentences.en: so every damn thing in that house, almost everything, was green.
sentences.zh: 所以那房子里该死的每一样东西，几乎所有东西，都是绿色的。

sentences.en: The main bathroom was green.
sentences.zh: 主浴室是绿色的。

sentences.en: The living room, kitchen was painted green.
sentences.zh: 客厅、厨房都漆成了绿色。

sentences.en: Never has a style and color complemented each other so perfectly
sentences.zh: 从来没有哪种风格和颜色能像

sentences.en: as mid-century modern and avocado green.
sentences.zh: 世纪中期现代风格和牛油果绿那样完美契合。

sentences.en: And then there were steps going down to this basement.
sentences.zh: 然后还有通往地下室的楼梯。

sentences.en: The basement was the full length of the house.
sentences.zh: 地下室和房子一样长。

sentences.en: That basement was so big,
sentences.zh: 那个地下室太大了，

sentences.en: we would do races on bikes and scooters and wagons and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 我们会在里面骑自行车、滑板车、拉着小车比赛之类的。

sentences.en: We were going around the stairs.
sentences.zh: 我们绕着楼梯跑。

sentences.en: It was like the chariot race in Ben-Hur or something like that.
sentences.zh: 就像《宾虚》里的战车比赛一样。

sentences.en: In an Ebony magazine feature from 1971 titled Atlanta, Black Mecca of the South,
sentences.zh: 在1971年《乌木》杂志一篇题为《亚特兰大：南方的黑人麦加》的专题报道中，

sentences.en: Collier Heights was described as one of just a few verdant neighborhoods
sentences.zh: 科利尔高地被描述为仅有的几个郁郁葱葱的社区之一，

sentences.en: that are the true pride and joy of the city's black citizenry.
sentences.zh: 是该市黑人市民真正的骄傲和喜悦。

sentences.en: The neighborhood had also become a who's who of successful black Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 这个社区也成为了亚特兰大成功黑人的聚集地。

sentences.en: If you was anybody or somebody that had a dollar, you lived in Collier Heights.
sentences.zh: 如果你是有头有脸或者有钱的人，你就住在科利尔高地。

sentences.en: All doctors, you could find them in Collier Heights.
sentences.zh: 所有的医生，你都能在科利尔高地找到他们。

sentences.en: All preachers that had their big churches in Collier Heights.
sentences.zh: 所有在科利尔高地拥有大型教堂的牧师也是如此。

sentences.en: My tour guide, Clarence Luckett, one of his mentors was Reverend Martin Luther King, Sr.
sentences.zh: 我的导游克拉伦斯·卢克特，他的导师之一就是马丁·路德·金牧师的父亲。

sentences.en: Around Collier Heights, they call him Daddy King.
sentences.zh: 在科利尔高地，人们叫他“金爸爸”。

sentences.en: He had a house there.
sentences.zh: 他在那里有一栋房子。

sentences.en: And so did Ralph Abernathy, the civil rights leader who was a best friend and close advisor
sentences.zh: 拉尔夫·阿伯内西也有一栋，他是民权领袖，也是马丁·路德·金博士的挚友和亲密顾问。

sentences.en: to Martin Luther King, Jr.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金博士的挚友和亲密顾问。

sentences.en: Manette Coleman's dad was George Coleman, editor of the Atlanta Daily World,
sentences.zh: 米内特·科尔曼的父亲是乔治·科尔曼，《亚特兰大每日世界报》的编辑，

sentences.en: one of the oldest black newspapers in the country.
sentences.zh: 这是全国最古老的黑人报纸之一。

sentences.en: There was a bank president, at least two state congressmen, Grady Hospital's medical director,
sentences.zh: 那里住着银行行长、至少两位州议员、格雷迪医院的医疗主任，

sentences.en: several architects and lawyers.
sentences.zh: 还有几位建筑师和律师。

sentences.en: Myrna Clayton remembers her neighborhood got so famous for its illustrious residents and gorgeous homes,
sentences.zh: 米尔娜·克莱顿记得她的社区因为杰出的居民和华丽的住宅而变得非常出名，

sentences.en: it became a straight-up tourist attraction.
sentences.zh: 它直接变成了一个旅游景点。

sentences.en: When I was younger, tour buses used to come down the street.
sentences.zh: 我小时候，旅游巴士经常开进这条街。

sentences.en: People wanted to see, you know, Collier Heights.
sentences.zh: 人们想看看，你知道，科利尔高地。

sentences.en: And so I'd be waving at the bus going past, but there would be big greyhound-sized buses.
sentences.zh: 所以我经常对着经过的巴士挥手，那可是像灰狗巴士那么大的车。

sentences.en: Not everyone in Collier Heights was famous or part of the wealthy elite.
sentences.zh: 科利尔高地并非每个人都是名人或富有的精英。

sentences.en: Some were HBCU professors, laborers, clerks, and librarians.
sentences.zh: 有些人是历史悠久的黑人大学（HBCU）的教授、劳工、职员和图书管理员。

sentences.en: Some were strivers who scraped together just enough to buy themselves and their families,
sentences.zh: 有些人是奋斗者，他们省吃俭用，只为给自己和家人买下，

sentences.en: some of the good life out there.
sentences.zh: 在那里过上一点好日子。

sentences.en: A lot of those people got in those houses by doing jobs that were menial.
sentences.zh: 很多人是通过做一些卑微的工作才住进那些房子的。

sentences.en: They built up a business, but before that, you know, in college, a lot of them waited tables.
sentences.zh: 他们建立了自己的事业，但在那之前，你知道，在大学里，他们很多人都在餐厅端盘子。

sentences.en: Some of them may not have even gone to college.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至可能没上过大学。

sentences.en: Some of them had worked for white folks, saw how they lived, and said,
sentences.zh: 有些人曾为白人工作，看到了他们的生活方式，然后说，

sentences.en: hmm, this is how the better half lives, this is how I want to live.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是上层人的生活，这就是我想要的生活。

sentences.en: By the early 1970s, the community had grown to include 2,000 homes built from scratch.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪70年代初，该社区已发展到拥有2000栋从零开始建造的房屋。

sentences.en: This was peak Collier Heights.
sentences.zh: 这是科利尔高地的巅峰时期。

sentences.en: For the people who lived there, the neighborhood had become more than just a solution
sentences.zh: 对于住在这里的人来说，这个社区不仅仅是解决

sentences.en: to a housing crisis in a segregated city.
sentences.zh: 种族隔离城市中住房危机的方案。

sentences.en: Black folks wanted in on the suburban dream,
sentences.zh: 黑人们想要实现郊区梦想，

sentences.en: and Collier Heights had promised to make it come true tenfold.
sentences.zh: 而科利尔高地承诺让这个梦想成真十倍。

sentences.en: Along with peace and fresh air, this cloistered, all-Black suburb offered even a small break from white racism.
sentences.zh: 除了宁静和新鲜空气，这个与世隔绝的全黑人郊区甚至提供了一点点远离白人种族主义的喘息空间。

sentences.en: Collier Heights was also a space where some upwardly mobile Black people
sentences.zh: 科利尔高地也是一个让一些向上流动的黑人

sentences.en: could distinguish their community from lower-income neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 能够将他们的社区与低收入社区区分开来的空间。

sentences.en: And, in general, Black Atlanta was proud that a space so grand had been made for and by Black people.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，亚特兰大黑人为能由黑人亲手打造出如此宏伟的空间而感到自豪。

sentences.en: Collier Heights was also celebrated for showing the world a vision of Black progress.
sentences.zh: 科利尔高地也因向世界展示了黑人进步的愿景而受到赞誉。

sentences.en: Proof that Black folks wanted to and could live well, even luxuriously, in suburbia.
sentences.zh: 证明了黑人想要并且能够过上好日子，甚至是在郊区过上奢华的生活。

sentences.en: For its residents, Collier Heights represented the epitome of self-determination and dignity
sentences.zh: 对于居民来说，科利尔高地代表了自决和尊严的缩影。

sentences.en: in a world of entrenched anti-Blackness.
sentences.zh: 在一个根深蒂固的反黑人世界里。

sentences.en: A world where white Atlantans worked very hard to exclude them from certain communities.
sentences.zh: 在这个世界里，亚特兰大的白人竭尽全力将他们排斥在某些社区之外。

sentences.en: Black folks said, well, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 黑人们说，好吧，没关系。

sentences.en: You don't want to associate with us?
sentences.zh: 你们不想和我们往来？

sentences.en: Fine.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: We don't have to associate with you.
sentences.zh: 我们也不必和你们往来。

sentences.en: And we can survive and be okay.
sentences.zh: 我们可以生存下去，过得很好。

sentences.en: You know, and so we don't have to be in your world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以我们不必非得待在你们的世界里。

sentences.en: We'll create our own world.
sentences.zh: 我们会创造属于我们自己的世界。

sentences.en: We already know how to build.
sentences.zh: 我们本就懂得如何建设。

sentences.en: We know how to, we got the skills.
sentences.zh: 我们知道怎么做，我们有这方面的技能。

sentences.en: Black people get a lot of hand-me-downs.
sentences.zh: 黑人总是得到很多别人剩下的东西。

sentences.en: From laws and legislations, to clothes and shoes and everything like that.
sentences.zh: 从法律法规，到衣服鞋子，诸如此类的一切。

sentences.en: My parents deserved a brand new house.
sentences.zh: 我的父母理应拥有一栋全新的房子。

sentences.en: They deserved new.
sentences.zh: 他们理应拥有全新的东西。

sentences.en: They deserved everything that that house had to offer.
sentences.zh: 他们理应拥有那栋房子所能提供的一切。

sentences.en: A good neighborhood, good schools, close to the church, and a house that didn't come
sentences.zh: 一个好的社区，好的学校，离教堂很近，还有一栋没有承载

sentences.en: with somebody else's memories.
sentences.zh: 别人记忆的房子。

sentences.en: They created everything in there on their own.
sentences.zh: 那里的一切都是他们亲手创造的。

sentences.en: In 2009, nearly 50 years after the Colemans moved into their home, Collier Heights was
sentences.zh: 2009年，在科尔曼一家搬进他们家近50年后，科利尔高地被

sentences.en: listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
sentences.zh: 列入了国家史迹名录。

sentences.en: The community was officially not new anymore.
sentences.zh: 这个社区在官方层面已经不再是“新”的了。

sentences.en: It was also a lot smaller than it used to be.
sentences.zh: 它也比过去小了很多。

sentences.en: The neighborhood boundaries were redrawn, shrinking Collier Heights down to a historic core that's
sentences.zh: 社区边界被重新划分，科利尔高地被缩减为一个历史核心区，

sentences.en: less than a quarter of its original size.
sentences.zh: 面积不到其原始规模的四分之一。

sentences.en: There have been other changes, too.
sentences.zh: 这里也发生了一些其他变化。

sentences.en: In recent decades, some residents have put ornate, wrought iron bars on their windows
sentences.zh: 近几十年来，一些居民为了安全，在窗户和门上

sentences.en: and doors for safety.
sentences.zh: 安装了华丽的锻铁栅栏。

sentences.en: Lawns have gotten a bit shaggy, and some of the houses could stand a little TLC.
sentences.zh: 草坪变得有些杂乱，有些房子也需要好好修缮一番。

sentences.en: ...back of his house.
sentences.zh: ……他房子的后面。

sentences.en: And he had a big old swimming pool in the back of his house.
sentences.zh: 他房子的后面有一个很大的旧游泳池。

sentences.en: And these were the so-called elite black folks with some duckies in there.
sentences.zh: 这些所谓的黑人精英们，里面还养着小鸭子。

sentences.en: As Clarence Luckett drives me around, pointing out this doctor's home here and that lawyer's
sentences.zh: 当克拉伦斯·拉基带我四处参观，指着这位医生的家，又指着那边那位律师的

sentences.en: house over there, we talk about probably the biggest change in Collier Heights, its greatest
sentences.zh: 房子时，我们谈到了科利尔高地可能发生的最大变化，它最伟大的

sentences.en: resource, that first generation of homeowners, is passing away.
sentences.zh: 资源——第一代房主们，正在相继离世。

sentences.en: Sometimes the younger generations can't or don't really want to take care of the house,
sentences.zh: 有时年轻一代无法或并不真的想打理这些房子，

sentences.en: which can lead to neglect.
sentences.zh: 这会导致房屋荒废。

sentences.en: Now, this is the doctor's house over the right.
sentences.zh: 看，右边那栋就是医生的房子。

sentences.en: He's the one that built all of these.
sentences.zh: 这些房子都是他建的。

sentences.en: He's dead, and his family won't move in the house.
sentences.zh: 他去世了，他的家人也不愿搬进这栋房子。

sentences.en: But you see how it's weeded up a little.
sentences.zh: 但你看，那里已经长了一些杂草。

sentences.en: Many of those kids have their own homes, and they're not interested in living in Collier
sentences.zh: 许多孩子都有了自己的房子，他们对住在科利尔

sentences.en: Heights.
sentences.zh: 高地不感兴趣。

sentences.en: Manette Coleman explains that parents like hers wanted their kids to be among the best educated
sentences.zh: 马内特·科尔曼解释说，像她父母那样的家长希望他们的孩子能接受最好的教育，

sentences.en: to get great jobs and to have zero limits on where they could travel and live.
sentences.zh: 找到好工作，并且在旅行和居住地选择上不受任何限制。

sentences.en: The plan worked, and for a while, it was hard to convince those kids and other younger
sentences.zh: 这个计划奏效了，有一段时间，很难说服那些孩子和其他年轻

sentences.en: families to move back to the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 家庭搬回社区。

sentences.en: You see houses that went up for sale, and nobody has bought them because they look like mansions,
sentences.zh: 你会看到有些房子挂牌出售，却没人买，因为它们看起来像豪宅，

sentences.en: but nobody who wants to live in a mansion wants to live in Collier Heights.
sentences.zh: 但想住豪宅的人并不想住在科利尔高地。

sentences.en: But that's changing, too.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况也在改变。

sentences.en: Manette's family just sold their home to a man who has big plans to renovate.
sentences.zh: 马内特的家人刚把房子卖给了一个有宏大翻新计划的人。

sentences.en: Neighbors say they're seeing more and more strangers, both black and white, pass through
sentences.zh: 邻居们说，他们看到越来越多的陌生人，无论是黑人还是白人，穿梭在

sentences.en: the community, not tourists, but people who want to buy.
sentences.zh: 社区里，他们不是游客，而是想买房的人。

sentences.en: With as much intention as it took to build this jewel of the black Mecca, Clarence Luckey
sentences.zh: 克拉伦斯·拉基认为，正如当初建立这个黑人麦加圣地需要极大的决心一样，

sentences.en: believes they've got to preserve it by retelling and handing down the epic of Collier Heights.
sentences.zh: 他们必须通过重述和传承科利尔高地的史诗来保护它。

sentences.en: It's going to have to be parents like me, let their kids know there always should be a home house,
sentences.zh: 这得靠像我这样的父母，让孩子们知道，这里永远应该有一个家，

sentences.en: an old church that you can bring.
sentences.zh: 一个你可以带人回来的老教堂。

sentences.en: Your great-great-grand said, this is where grandmama lived.
sentences.zh: 你的曾曾祖父母会说，这就是奶奶住过的地方。

sentences.en: Collier Heights might not have the conveniences of a trendy Atlanta neighborhood, but what gives
sentences.zh: 科利尔高地可能没有亚特兰大时尚社区的便利设施，但赋予

sentences.en: this community its weight is that powerful origin story, everything that went into carving
sentences.zh: 这个社区分量的，是那段强大的起源故事，是开辟出这片

sentences.en: out a space that was, as the locals say, for us, by us.
sentences.zh: 正如当地人所说，“为我们，由我们”打造的空间所付出的一切。

sentences.en: Now, you take my daddy, he was born in 1898, maybe.
sentences.zh: 你看我爸爸，他大概是1898年出生的。

sentences.en: My granddaddy was a slave.
sentences.zh: 我爷爷是个奴隶。

sentences.en: They didn't have nowhere to go back to to show their kids, see?
sentences.zh: 他们没有地方可以回去展示给孩子们看，明白吗？

sentences.en: So, what we have to tell our kids about this neighborhood is the history of what your
sentences.zh: 所以，我们必须告诉孩子们关于这个社区的事，就是你们的

sentences.en: grandparents had to do just to live in this neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 祖父母为了住进这个社区所必须付出的努力的历史。

sentences.en: The only way things can be history, somebody got to pass it on.
sentences.zh: 事物要成为历史，就必须有人传承下去。

sentences.en: When we come back for the COTA, we're going to talk about the thing that all people talk
sentences.zh: 当我们从COTA回来后，我们要谈谈所有人在郊区都会谈论的事情，

sentences.en: about in the suburbs, even historic, groundbreaking suburbs.
sentences.zh: 即使是在那些历史悠久、开创性的郊区也是如此。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about lawns after this.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们将讨论草坪问题。

sentences.en: We're back with Christopher Johnson.
sentences.zh: 我们回到了克里斯托弗·约翰逊身边。

sentences.en: Hey, Christopher.
sentences.zh: 嘿，克里斯托弗。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: So, obviously, I went to Atlanta to work on this story, and this was my first time out
sentences.zh: 显然，我去亚特兰大做这个报道，这是我自新冠封锁以来第一次

sentences.en: in the field since the COVID lockdowns.
sentences.zh: 到实地采访。

sentences.en: And so, what was that like?
sentences.zh: 那感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: What did you do?
sentences.zh: 你做了些什么？

sentences.en: One of my first stops was barbecue.
sentences.zh: 我第一站去吃的是烧烤。

sentences.en: I hope that's all right.
sentences.zh: 希望没问题。

sentences.en: That's perfectly fine.
sentences.zh: 完全没问题。

sentences.en: But I also got to hang out in Collier Heights, which was really great, because I got to meet
sentences.zh: 但我也有机会在科利尔高地待了一段时间，这真的很棒，因为我见到

sentences.en: some pretty wonderful people and just spend some time.
sentences.zh: 了一些非常棒的人，并和他们共度了时光。

sentences.en: Some folks, I sat down with them in their living rooms, and we just talked, classic Southern
sentences.zh: 我坐在一些人的客厅里，我们只是聊天，这就是经典的南方

sentences.en: hospitality.
sentences.zh: 待客之道。

sentences.en: And in the course of talking to a lot of different people, I came across a whole other part of
sentences.zh: 在与许多不同的人交谈的过程中，我发现了关于科利尔高地这个故事的

sentences.en: this story about Collier Heights that I didn't get to talk about earlier.
sentences.zh: 另一个层面，这是我之前没能谈到的。

sentences.en: As I chatted with some folks there, people who are from Collier Heights, people who grew
sentences.zh: 当我与那里的一些人聊天时，那些来自科利尔高地的人，那些在

sentences.en: up there, there was one thing kept coming up over and over again, which was lawn care.
sentences.zh: 那里长大的人，有一件事被反复提及，那就是草坪护理。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 呵。

sentences.en: Okay, this is interesting.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这很有意思。

sentences.en: Lawns are very fraught subjects when it comes to home ownership, so I'm intrigued to how
sentences.zh: 草坪在房屋所有权方面是一个非常敏感的话题，所以我很好奇它在科利尔高地

sentences.en: the flavor of it in Collier Heights.
sentences.zh: 是什么样的风味。

sentences.en: A lot of it was prompted by me asking people how Collier Heights had changed in the last
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上是因为我问人们科利尔高地在过去

sentences.en: few decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年里发生了什么变化。

sentences.en: And the grass kept coming up over and over again.
sentences.zh: 而草坪问题被反复提起。

sentences.en: So, for example, you remember Myrna Clayton from this story.
sentences.zh: 比如，你还记得这个故事里的默娜·克莱顿吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, she's our opening anecdote.
sentences.zh: 记得，她是我们的开篇人物。

sentences.en: She's the one who's like, dad bought her a house in Collier Heights because she had
sentences.zh: 就是那个说她爸爸在科利尔高地给她买了一栋房子，因为她在那里度过了

sentences.en: just magical sleepovers there.
sentences.zh: 非常美妙的留宿时光的人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That Myrna Clayton.
sentences.zh: 就是那个默娜·克莱顿。

sentences.en: So, I asked her about changes in the community in the last few decades, and one of her issues
sentences.zh: 所以我问她社区在过去几十年里的变化，她提到的问题之一

sentences.en: was the grass and neighbors just not taking care of their front lawns anymore.
sentences.zh: 就是草坪，邻居们不再打理他们的前院草坪了。

sentences.en: People parking on grass, that's not something that we did.
sentences.zh: 把车停在草坪上，这不是我们做过的事。

sentences.en: You know, people not cutting their grass, it's just not something we did.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们不割草，这根本不是我们做过的事。

sentences.en: You know, we always took care of our lawns, you know, where that's just not something that
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们总是打理我们的草坪，你知道，这只是很多人

sentences.zh: 不知道该怎么做而已。

sentences.zh: 是的，我以前听过这个说法。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，草坪护理或者说缺乏护理，可能是最典型的郊区抱怨了。

sentences.zh: 这促使许多社区协会去起草关于维护的章程，

sentences.zh: 以及各种各样的规定来控制人们及其对草坪的处理方式。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: It's a huge thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件大事。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.zh: 这很大程度上关乎阶级价值观。

sentences.zh: 所以，比如在科利尔高地，从一开始，这个社区就是亚特兰大

sentences.zh: 中产阶级和上层阶级的空间。

sentences.en: And one of the things that held that together is middle and upper class values.
